quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors?

options.text: Check them regularly as part of your normal driving routine.
Avoid checking them because they distract you.
Avoid checking them because other drivers can see you.
Only check them in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check them regularly as part of your normal driving routine.
questions.explanation: You need to know what is behind you. Check your mirrors often as part of your regular scanning routine.

questions.question: Where should you find information about your motorcycle?

options.text: The owner's manual.
A general book about motorcycles.
Someone who owns a different type of motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before you ride your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle.

questions.question: What is the best source for information about your motorcycle?

options.text: The owner's manual.
A book about motorcycles.
A former owner.
Someone who knows about motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is your best source for information about your specific motorcycle. It includes details about how to operate your motorcycle and how to maintain it.

questions.question: When you brake on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use either brake, but never both together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when you stop. Using both brakes at once gives you the best stopping power.

questions.question: What is true about clothing for motorcycle riding?

options.text: Clothing should be loose enough to flap in the wind.
You do not need to cover your arms or legs completely.
You should not wear a jacket in warm weather.
Good clothing can protect you if you crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Good clothing can protect you if you crash.
questions.explanation: The right clothing protects you in a crash. Always wear a jacket and long pants that cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. Your clothes should fit snugly without flapping but should not restrict your movement.

questions.question: Which item does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?

options.text: A leather jacket
Boots that cover your ankles
A baseball cap that fits snugly
Gloves

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap that fits snugly
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high ankle boots or shoes, and durable gloves to protect yourself from injury.

questions.question: Are low-speed motorcycle crashes dangerous?

options.text: Yes, they can be fatal.
No, they are never serious.
No, they rarely cause injuries.
No, they happen often, so you should not worry about them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they can be fatal.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds below 30 miles per hour. Even slow crashes can cause serious injury or death.

questions.question: What is the correct way to pass another vehicle?

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may complete the pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
You should honk your horn to make the other driver slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: All passing must be done at legal speeds and only where it is safe and legal to pass.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on bridge grating?

options.text: Always ride on the far right side of the lane.
Always ride on the far left side of the lane.
Slowly zigzag across the grating.
Stay calm, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle may weave slightly on grating or rain grooves. This is usually harmless, so just stay calm and continue at a steady speed. Do not try to zigzag because this is dangerous and causes you to drift across your lane.

questions.question: What type of clothing helps other drivers see you?

options.text: Dark-colored clothes
Clothes made from synthetic materials
Reflective clothes
A leather jacket

questions.correctAnswerText: Reflective clothes
questions.explanation: Wear bright, reflective gear so other drivers can see you and your motorcycle.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Let them ride.
Tell them to take less-crowded roads.
Push their bike over.
Get other friends to help talk them out of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to help talk them out of riding.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has been drinking to ride. Do everything you can to stop them. Ask other friends to help convince them not to ride.

questions.question: What do goggles protect?

options.text: Only your eyes.
Your eyes just as well as a face shield.
Your face as well as a windshield.
Your entire face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only your eyes.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect only your eyes, not your whole face. A face shield is better because it protects your entire face. A windshield does not provide the same protection as a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: What is another name for shifting to a lower gear?

options.text: Engine braking.
Acceleration.
Upshifting.
Coasting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Engine braking.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle like brakes do. This is why downshifting is also called engine braking.

questions.question: What is an advantage of keeping a group of riders small?

options.text: A small group is harder for traffic to separate than a larger group.
A small group can break traffic laws to stay together.
Riders will always need to catch up to the group.
It will be hard to keep track of where everyone is.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group is harder for traffic to separate than a larger group.
questions.explanation: Small groups have several advantages. Other vehicles can pass them more safely. Traffic and stop lights are less likely to separate them. Slower riders do not have to rush to keep up.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders look over their shoulders before changing lanes?

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like all vehicles.
It gets the attention of other drivers.
Mirrors do not really help.
You should make eye contact with surrounding drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Always turn your head to check for vehicles or hazards in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Other drivers may be going slowly to look for a parking spot.
The road surface may be uneven.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: Riding next to parked cars is dangerous. A driver might pull out of a parking space without looking. Car doors may open into your lane. Pedestrians may step out from between cars.

questions.question: Can clothing help prevent injuries in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing does not protect.
No, clothing is just a personal choice.
Yes, but only if your clothes are very loose and flap in the wind.
Yes, if your jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if your jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Good clothing can reduce injury in a crash. Choose a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, are made of strong material, and fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What is the rule for passing in a no passing zone?

options.text: A motorcycle may still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass if no other vehicle is coming.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in no passing zones. You cannot pass by riding off the main road either.

questions.question: Why should you keep an adequate distance behind other vehicles?

options.text: To give yourself time and space to notice and react to hazards.
So you can tailgate.
So traffic counters can count you as a vehicle.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give yourself time and space to notice and react to hazards.
questions.explanation: A good following distance gives you enough space to stop or swerve if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. It also helps you see road hazards ahead, like potholes.

questions.question: What happens if your motorcycle's chain or belt breaks?

options.text: The rear wheel suddenly gets more power.
The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly gets more power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
questions.explanation: If your drive chain or belt breaks, the rear wheel will suddenly lose power.

questions.question: When you adjust your rearview mirror, what should you be able to see?

options.text: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
Only the lane behind you.
Only the lane next to you.
Most of your helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you. The road behind and to the side of you is most important to see.

questions.question: When downshifting, what should you do?

options.text: Shift through multiple gears at once.
Shift through one gear at a time.
Always shift all the way to neutral first.
Accelerate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift through one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: When downshifting, shift down one gear at a time. Ease out the clutch slowly between each downshift.

questions.question: What is true about an approved helmet?

options.text: It lets you see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
It looks good.
It does not have a chin strap.
It protects your hearing.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets you see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet will let you see as far as you need for safe riding. It does not limit your side vision.

questions.question: Which sign is usually rectangular?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are usually rectangular. They have white backgrounds with black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.
